study.question: Does count-dependent retrieval magnitude improve the unsuccessful iterative field/history exchange model beyond an explicit history-length feature, and does its effect depend on refreshing queries from retrieved evidence?
study.hypothesis: Observation: baseline-din click AUC=0.65554408 exceeds all four exchange cells (0.63229720..0.64745824). With writing enabled, refreshing queries adds 0.00200171 AUC; with refresh enabled, writing adds 0.00671789; their single-seed difference-in-differences is -0.00644144. These are descriptive matched contrasts, not repeated support. The best exchange is worse than DIN in every declared history-length slice, including empty histories, so history pooling cannot explain the whole deficit. Inspected exchange source uses sum-one reads over a 32-dimensional event bottleneck, whereas DIN retains full item/action values and unconstrained local weights. Mechanism hypothesis: averaging away prefix-dependent read magnitude can limit how retrieved evidence changes field states and their next queries. A square-root visible-count multiplier at both reads may restore a useful multiplicative path, beyond providing the count to prediction towers. This is one admissible explanation of failure, not evidence that compression or normalization caused it.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text arXiv:1706.06978v4 lines272-277 explicitly motivates abandoning softmax normalization to preserve interest intensity. This experiment retains softmax relative weights and multiplies them by sqrt(visible count), rather than using learned unnormalized DIN activation scores; visible count is not target-specific learned interest intensity. It embeds that test in an iterative field/history structure. No DIN reproduction or originality claim.

Pinned90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d source lines158-282 repeats cross-attention and mixed FFNs with token-specific Q/output projections. We retain the previous shared-projection field/history exchange, strictly mask padded scores, keep its affine feedback write, and test retrieval magnitude x feedback query. Original EST paper detail is unavailable through the authorized archive; novelty relative to it remains unverified.

Pinned benchmark source lines188-217 alternates hub aggregation and affine broadcast; lines222-249 document mask-free aggregation with zeroed sequence K/V. Our inherited writer is a shared field-mean-conditioned affine residual, with strictly masked reads, no task hubs and no task-mask routing. This follow-up adds only count-dependent read magnitude and a count feature; it does not reproduce INFNet.

study.proposed_difference: At each of the two field-to-history reads, multiply masked, renormalized softmax weights by sqrt(n) in M1, or by1 in M0, where n is the number of visible history events. Relative attention weights remain identical before downstream feedback effects. Expose log1p(n)/log(101) to every task tower in every cell. Cross M with second-read query source Q: first_fields (refreshed) vs first_query (static). Both query groups retain the first-read evidence through the second field mixer and writer; Q isolates an additional query path, not all history feedback. This is a mechanism diagnostic continuing an unsuccessful trajectory, not a claimed new model contribution. No compression-width or optimizer change.
predictions: Primary predeclared contrast: click AUC(mass_m1_q1) > click AUC(mass_m0_q1), with equal learned capacity and explicit count in both.

If count-scaled evidence specifically helps query/evidence co-evolution, the M1-M0 click AUC contrast should be larger for Q1 than Q0. A main effect without that interaction supports only a read-magnitude effect, not a query-feedback mechanism.

Report all four AUC/Logloss values and auxiliary mean separately; click AUC selects. Compare the best new cell with baseline-din as a performance reference; failure to exceed0.65554408 means DIN remains incumbent even if within-family effects improve.

Reuse predeclared history bins empty,1-16,17-64,>64. Expected benefit should occur with nonempty histories, not be inferred from a changed overall history mix. Report sample/positive/negative counts and mark insufficient bins. Existing validation counts: empty6444/427/6017;1-16:461684/28818/432866;17-64:1001754/55298/946456;>64:1401885/50957/1350928. Training-induced empty-slice differences remain possible; n=0 must give an exact zero read in either mode for fixed parameters.

Within-cell fixed-parameter host checks: valid attention sum=1 for M0 or sqrt(n) for M1, zero for n=0; n=1 modes coincide, masked-value perturbations do not change predictions, finite outputs/backward for empty/mixed/full prefixes. Collect host parameter/cost/memory/throughput/latency metrics; no efficiency claim from equal pass counts alone.
falsifiers: M1Q1 does not beat M0Q1 on full validation click AUC: this square-root count implementation is unsupported under the frozen recipe. Do not call normalization or iterative exchange refuted generally.
The M effect is no greater at Q1 than Q0: reject evidence for positive coupling to query refresh, even if an overall M gain exists.

Comparable gain only in normalized-plus-count controls relative to historical cells, with no M advantage: explicit count or changed tower/optimization is sufficient at this resolution; historical comparisons also change initialization shape and cannot isolate count causally.

Nonfinite host forward/backward, incorrect mask behavior, invalid source/interface or trial-cap overrun invalidates the affected run; retain failed costs and do not interpret execution failures scientifically.
A future paired-seed reversal or equal-cost disadvantage weakens a provisional one-seed improvement; one run cannot establish a general mechanism.
alternative_explanations: The32-dimensional event projection may lose field/action information, and normalized values/field mixers may dominate; this study does not isolate compression.

Count-dependent scaling may merely improve optimization or residual branch balance in the fixed single-pass, low-dense-learning-rate recipe. Even a positive factorial interaction does not exclude this. A later constant-gain replacement with equal count features is needed before attributing gains specifically to per-user intensity.

History length correlates with prevalence, user activity and truncation. n counts only the released visible prefix, capped100; it cannot establish long-term preference intensity or production causal validity.

The explicit count feature adds512 dense weights versus old exchange models and changes tower initialization shape; comparisons with old trials are context, not exact count-only contrasts. Within the four new cells all modules, active capacity and initialization order match.
Single-seed variation, task sharing, calibration and the inherited offline feedback maturity assumptions can explain apparent gains; no withheld assessment is authorized in this phase.
